articles.title: Jia Zhangke Readies Zhao Tao Road Movie ‘Mamma Dunhuang,’ Rules Out AI in Production (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Jia Zhangke will turn his attention to location scouting and production design for his next film, road movie “Mamma Dunhuang,” once the 10th Pingyao Crouching Tiger Hidden Dragon International Film Festival wraps on Sept. 30.
body: Zhao Tao, who won the David di Donatello Award for best actress for “Shun Li and the Poet,” will once again lead a Jia film, playing a homebound woman who uses AI to help her on the journey.
“I will not use AI in making ‘Mamma Dunhuang,'” Jia says. “It only plays a role in the story.”

Jia founded the Pingyao festival, which marks its 10th edition this year. He says that although it’s only been a decade, “the changes in the broader film ecosystem and the media landscape, as well as technological advancements, are drastic. Pingyao has remained nimble. We’ve been able to adapt continuously alongside the shifts in the film industry and surrounding media, capturing new developments for our curation. Looking ahead, I believe cinema will continue to evolve rapidly, so we will maintain this festival’s agility in the future. That very flexibility allows us to respond in real time to the most pressing cinematic and cultural topics on people’s minds today.”

articles.title: Welcome To Space College: How Do You Join Starfleet Academy On Star Trek?
articles.summary: Starfleet Academy has been referenced in Star Trek since its inception, but what does the admissions process actually look like? Here's what it takes to get in.
body: Welcome to Trekspertise, a series where we break down the technology, history, details, and decisions that make the Star Trek universe so complex — and so fun.

The latest "Star Trek" series, "Star Trek: Starfleet Academy," debuted in January of 2026, but it has already been canceled, with plans to air its second and final season sometime in 2027. It's a pity it didn't last very long, as a series set at Starfleet Academy has been a long time coming. One of the "Star Trek" head honchos, Harve Bennett, was brainstorming a "Starfleet Academy" series way back in the early 1980s, and the franchise has drifted that direction many times. Even a tie-in novel series was set there.

Throughout the franchise, there have been multiple mentions of the types of classes that officers need to take at Starfleet Academy. Naturally, one has to know astrophysics, basic warp design, engineering, and xenolinguistics, but one must also take courses in probability mechanics, interspecies ethics, advanced subspace geometry, and even comparative xenomythology.
How does one apply to Starfleet Academy? It seems that's just as hard.

articles.title: Celebrity Traitors 2 cast: Who are this year's 'big dogs' and dark horses?
articles.summary: The reality TV game show returns on Thursday, with 21 stars vying to win £100,000 for their chosen charity.
body: Celebrity Traitors returns next week for a second round of deception and amateur detective work.

Hosted by Claudia Winkleman, the Traitors castle will welcome 21 new celebrities on Thursday, as a group of famous "faithfuls" attempts to work out which among them are - and perhaps, always have been - "traitors", secretly murdering contestants each night.

Last year's show provided Bafta's most memorable TV moment - an award voted for by the British public - when traitor Alan Carr broke down in tears at the end of the final having bluffed his way to a win by hiding in plain sight.
Let's have a stab in the dark, then, at who might follow in Jonathan Ross's footsteps as this year's "big dog", and who, like singer Cat Burns, could fly under the radar?

articles.title: The 10 Best Rivalries in Video Game History, Ranked
articles.summary: A classic rivalry between two distinct, memorable characters has been a staple of narrative storytelling long before the advent of video games, yet something about the medium of gaming has made it perfect for the concept and longevity of many memorable rivalries.
body: It further helps that these rivalries don't just stand out for one amazing game, but have evolved and grown across generations of gaming in some of the biggest franchises in gaming history. Gaming as an art form simply wouldn't be the same without these rivalries, whether they be fan favorites of hardcore gamers or instantly recognizable to even those not as familiar with video games. Even as new games and effective rivalries are released, it's difficult to imagine any of them coming close to the strength of these iconic rivalries.

For a game series all about defending clients in the court of law, it only makes sense that there would be a consistent rivalry between Ace Attorney series protagonist Phoenix Wright and the leading prosecutor, Miles Edgeworth. However, their actions and battles in court only scratch the surface of the dynamic between these two, as they have grown up as childhood friends and see their rivalry as a way to further drive and invigorate their work. Their rivalry and friendship grow especially deeper as the games go on, bringing out the best in one another both in terms of their work and character.

articles.title: One of the Greatest Sci-Fi Nightmares Ever Made Is Officially Streaming for Free
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence is perennially in the news at the moment, isn't it? The threat of it becoming sentient is very topical, so imagine giving it a face, locking it underground, and asking a lonely programmer to determine whether it can manipulate him. It feels like actively tempting fate.
body: Ex Machina, the directorial debut from acclaimed screenwriter Alex Garland, is officially free to stream this month via the Roku Channel, bringing one of the 21st century’s best sci-fi thrillers back within very easy reach. Caleb Smith, a programmer at a huge Internet company, wins a contest that enables him to spend a week at the private estate of Nathan Bateman, his firm’s brilliant CEO. When he arrives, Caleb learns that he has been chosen to be the human component in a Turing test to determine the capabilities and consciousness of Ava, a beautiful robot. However, it soon becomes evident that Ava is far more self-aware and deceptive than either man imagined.

The cast is deliberately tiny, with Domhnall Gleeson ( Star Wars: The Force Awakens ) joined by Oscar Isaac ( Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker ) as Nathan, Alicia Vikander ( Tomb Raider ) as Ava, and Sonoya Mizuno ( House of the Dragon ) as Kyoko. Corey Johnson ( The Mummy ) also appears as Jay, while Claire Selby, Gana Bayarsaikhan, and Tiffany Pisani round out the ensemble.

body: Radio presenter Owain Wyn Evans will cycle through all four UK nations to raise money for BBC Children in Need.
The five-day challenge will start on Monday, 9 November, and finish on Friday, 13 November - when the fundraiser will be broadcast.
The only member of the annual TV fundraiser's hosting team for 2026 to be revealed so far is fellow Welsh presenter, One Show host Alex Jones.
The BBC said Evans' challenge would be the "greatest ever distance" covered in a Radio 2 endeavour for the charity.

The original movie, which qualifies as one of the earliest “ mock-busters ” in history, was an unauthorized adaptation of Stoker’s work, but it earned respect in its own right. Directed by the visionary F.W. Murnau, the movie follows a Dracula stand-in named Count Orlok, played by Max Schreck. The role was played by Klaus Kinski in a 1973 remake directed by Werner Herzog, and by Bill Skarsgård in Eggers’ film. A movie about the making of the 1922 classic, titled Shadow of the Vampire, featured John Malkovich as Murnau and Willem Dafoe as Schreck.
Four franchises, four completely different ways of getting underneath your skin. This is the one built out of your particular fear, why it works so well on you, and what it would leave behind.
